humanTitle: People cannot turn off the prompts that slow their editor
whoItAffects: iPhone users in the United States and Australia, across two app versions.

build.proposition: A preference that stops the prompt loading, not just showing.
specifics: Gate the feature’s code path, not only its dialog
Remember the answer per document, not per session
Measure open time with the path disabled, and publish both
build.limitation: A feature the company is promoting is rarely one it will let people switch off.

start.proposition: A drawing tool whose feature set is fixed by the person using it.
specifics: Version pinning, so an editor cannot change under a deadline
Aimed at people who open the same document every working day
start.limitation: Holding old code paths open is expensive, and the people who want it are the least likely to pay more for it.

study.proposition: Does an unrequested prompt change how long people stay in a document?
specifics: Compare session length either side of the version that added it
Separate the time it costs from the irritation it causes
study.limitation: The reviews report both at once, and nobody writes a review about the session they quietly abandoned.

write.proposition: The software you rent changed while you were using it.
specifics: Follow one document opened across the two versions reviewers name
Quote the reviewer asking for a switch, every time, on every file
write.limitation: Complaints about added features are a familiar genre, and this one needs the slowdown measured to rise above it.
